Personally I recall the writing in Baldur's Gate to have been somewhat perfunctory. Baldur's Gate II had much improved writing, and Planescape: Torment put them both to shame.

Baldur's Gate was a huge deal because it was the first Dungeons & Dragons CRPG since the "death" of RPGs when the Gold Box Series went kaput. It even had multiplayer so you could play through a D&D adventure online with your friends! And it was even a pretty good adventure at that. But I'm not sure it's writing stood out as a high point initially. It was adequate, and had it's moments, but didn't consistently wow anybody.

But, clearly this open to interpretation. The thrust of my point is that the writing for this expansion isn't even as good as the writing for the first game in the series, which set a minimum standard for RPG writing that has steadily gone up from there.
